body:
A connector can now move its items back from a type you mapped one of its kinds onto before, so changing a mapping no longer strands them.

### Server
- **Added:** Each entry in `rewrites` from `GET /plugins/{name}/connector/mapping` names `from`: for each kind, the types the rewrite moves the connector's items from. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)
- **Changed:** Exports and backups are now archive version 4. They carry each connector's former mapped types and its open rewrite requests, so a rewrite on a restored instance still moves every item back. A restore still reads a version 3 archive. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/export-and-restore)
- **Fixed:** When you map a connector's kind onto a type, rewrite its items there, then map the kind back to its own type or onto another type, a new rewrite now moves the connector's items off the type the kind left. Before, the connector could not reach those items, and every later write for them was refused `type_not_permitted`. While the rewrite is open, the connector can list, read and move only its own items there, never yours or another source's, and its reach ends when it clears the request. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)

### CLI
- **Fixed:** `marfa plugins mapping rewrite --dry-run` counts the items a rewrite would move, and says "would move N onto TYPE". Before, it counted the items already on the target, which a rewrite never moves. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** The client's types include `from` on a connector mapping's rewrite requests.

**Upgrading:** Upgrading changes the database and first keeps a copy, `marfa.db.before-upgrade`; v0.0.100 can't open it afterwards. Exports and backups are now archive version 4, which v0.0.100 can't restore.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.100...v0.0.101

A filter that compares a list with a number or a boolean now matches the list's members, and built-in edge type labels are now in title case.

### Server
- **Changed:** Built-in edge type labels and reverse labels capitalize every word, as field labels do: `GET /edge-types` now returns `In Collection`, `Derived From` and `Subject Of` where it returned `In collection`, `Derived from` and `Subject of`. An app that matches on a label's text should match the new spelling, or better, on the edge type's `id`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/edges)
- **Fixed:** A filter that compares a property holding a list with a number or a boolean now tests the list's members, not the list's text. `properties.words eq 5` selects an item whose list holds `5`, `contains 5` selects the same items and no longer matches `[15]`, and `neq 5` selects a list that holds no `5`. A range such as `gt 4` still selects no list. Saved views that use such a filter may now list different items. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/list-filter-search)

### CLI
- **Changed:** The help for `marfa update start` and `marfa server upgrade` now says that a release opens the database of any earlier release from 0.0.86 on, except one 0.0.88 wrote, and upgrades it in place, keeping a copy first as `marfa.db.before-upgrade`.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A device's working copy answers a filter on a list with a number or a boolean the same way the server does.

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.99 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay at archive version 3, so v0.0.99 can restore an archive this release writes.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.99...v0.0.100

A connector can now sync onto the type you map its kind to, such as a tracker's issues onto your own tickets, and a plugin can say where its connector's code is.

### Server
- **Added:** A plugin's `connector` section can carry `code`: the `https` address of the connector's code file, its SHA-256 and its size. A connector host reads it from `GET /connector-hosts/self` to know what to fetch and to check the file before it runs it. It is optional, and the plugin's recorded fingerprint covers it.
- **Fixed:** A connector whose kind you map onto another type now syncs it. Its agreements cover its own items of the mapped type, and it can move its own items between the kind's type and the target type with `retype`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)
- **Fixed:** Saving a mapping with a new `target_type` and no `fields` fills the fields both types declare and no status overrides, where before the save was refused. A preview draft does the same.
- **Fixed:** A connector key can no longer move an item you made into its target type through `POST /items/bulk`; that is refused with `type_not_permitted`.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa plugins check` judges a connector's `code` section as installing does.

### Core
- **Added:** A device groups a saved view by whether a field is set, by status group across types and by source, and refuses a grouping it does not know with a message that names the setting. The server still refuses these groupings. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/working-copies)

**Upgrading:** The database is unchanged; a database from v0.0.98 opens as it is. Exports and backups stay archive version 3, so v0.0.98 can restore them.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.98...v0.0.99

You can now see the hidden data an app keeps in your Marfa and delete it, on its own or when you disconnect the app.

### Server
- **Added:** List the data an app keeps under its own `app.<vendor>` namespace with `GET /app-vendors/{vendor}/data`, and delete it with `DELETE /app-vendors/{vendor}/data`. Deleting purges the items and removes the app's types, so take a backup with `marfa backups run` first if you may want them back. Listing needs `grants.manage`, and deleting also needs `items.purge`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/see-and-revoke-access)
- **Added:** Delete an app's data in the same step that disconnects it, with `remove_data=true` on `DELETE /grants/{id}` and `DELETE /owner/sign-ins/{id}`. Disconnecting still keeps the data unless you ask.
- **Added:** The MCP admin tool `marfa_app_data` previews an app's data and deletes it once you confirm, and `marfa_end_sign_in` takes `remove_data`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** `GET /grants` names each app's namespaces, and `GET /app-vendors` names the app that holds each one.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa apps vendors data list <vendor>` shows an app's types and items, and `marfa apps vendors data delete <vendor> --confirm PURGE` deletes them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Added:** `marfa apps revoke` and `marfa sign-ins end` take `--remove-data --confirm PURGE` to delete the app's data as they disconnect it.
- **Changed:** `marfa apps list` shows each app's namespaces.

### Core
- **Added:** A device reads saved views grouped by whether a field is set, by status group and by source. The server accepts these groupings in a later release.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.97...v0.0.98

A filter on a property that holds a list now compares the list's members, so filtering by a tag-like list of words finds what it should.

### Server
- **Fixed:** A filter that compares a list property with text using `eq`, `contains` or `starts_with` now selects the items whose list holds a matching member. `properties.words eq "kitchen"` finds an item whose words include `kitchen`, where before it found nothing, and `contains` and `starts_with` match within one member, never within the list's JSON text. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/list-filter-search)
- **Fixed:** `neq` with text on a list property selects only the items whose list holds no member equal to the value, an empty list included. Before, it selected every item that held a list. Ranges, numbers, `exists` and `not_exists` behave as before.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A device's working copy and a saved view compare a list property's members in a filter, as the server does.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.96...v0.0.97

An agent can now read a type's guidance through Marfa's MCP server before it saves an item, and Marfa's own types ship with guidance on when to use each one.

### Server
- **Added:** `marfa_overview` returns a type's guidance, its ancestors' guidance and its status words' descriptions, and reads up to 20 types in one call when `type` is a list. A type it does not know is listed under `unknown`, and one whose stored definition cannot be read under `unreadable`, so one damaged type no longer hides the others. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Added:** `marfa_save_type` sets a type's guidance when it registers or changes a type, and an empty string removes it. It needs `schema.write`, as the API does.
- **Added:** `core.note`, `core.collection`, `core.task`, `core.bookmark`, `core.highlight` and `core.file` ship with guidance that says what each is for, what belongs in another type, and which links to write. Each shipped edge type's description now says which way the link runs. An instance picks the guidance up when it starts on this release. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/note)
- **Changed:** `GET /overview` and `marfa_overview` with no arguments name each type's `parent` and cut type and edge type descriptions at 200 characters instead of 100.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Changed:** The overview type in `@withmarfa/client` names `parent`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.95...v0.0.96

A plugin's connector can now write the links it needs and find its own items on a type the owner mapped one of its kinds onto, and every page of links is now full.

**Breaking:** A connector that answers a mapping preview must send `result` as `{ "type": <the kind's target type>, "properties": {…} }`, with optional `title` and `source_item`. Marfa now refuses any other form and names the path it refused, such as `result.type`.

### Server
- **Added:** A plugin's connector section can list the link (edge) types its connector writes in `edge_types`: the plugin's own, or ones Marfa ships such as `attached-to`. The key its host mints may write exactly those. A key minted before gets them the next time its host mints it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/plugin-format)
- **Added:** A connector's key reads its own items, and only its own, on a type the owner mapped one of its enabled kinds onto, through the requests it reconciles with: `GET /items`, `GET /events`, `POST /items/tombstones`, an item's read, links, history, extensions and table rows. Search, summaries, export, views, folders and MCP's read tools still answer as the key's type map says. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)
- **Changed:** A `text` setting of a plugin holds up to 65,536 characters. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/connector-settings)
- **Fixed:** A key that may read only some links no longer gets short or empty pages of links with a cursor to follow: every page but the last holds `limit` links. Links whose type was since deleted still appear on its pages.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa plugins check` refuses a connector's `edge_types` entry that is unknown, repeated, under a reserved name or ends on a system type, naming the entry. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/plugin-format)

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** `@withmarfa/client` types a connector's `edge_types` and a mapping preview's `result`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.94...v0.0.95

An owner can now link an instance to Marfa Cloud, which is in alpha, to give it a public name and address, sign a plugin's connector in to its provider through a browser, and pause a connector, run it now or preview its mapping.

### Server
- **Added:** An owner can link an instance to Marfa Cloud with `POST /cloud/link`, read the link with `GET /cloud/link` and unlink with `DELETE /cloud/link`, each with `config.manage`. A linked instance answers at its Marfa Cloud name through the tunnel connector each release carries, which runs only while the instance is linked. Nothing is sent to Marfa Cloud until the owner starts a link. Marfa Cloud is in alpha and sign-up is by invitation. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/marfa-cloud)
- **Added:** Linking moves the sign-in address to the Marfa Cloud name by default, once you confirm it, and unlinking puts the earlier address back. A key cannot confirm the move, so with a key the link is made and the move waits, and the link's status names the next step. `"sign_in_address": "keep"` leaves the address where it is.
- **Added:** A plugin's connector that declares a sign-in can get its refresh token through the owner's browser, with the owner's own OAuth client ID and secret kept in the plugin's settings. `POST /plugins/{name}/connector/sign-in` answers the address to open, and `GET` on the same path reads how the sign-in ended, with a fixed reason word when it failed. Marfa calls the provider only to finish a sign-in the owner started. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/connector-google-access)
- **Added:** An owner can pause a plugin's connector, resume it and ask it to run now with `POST /plugins/{name}/connector/pause`, `/resume` and `/run`. Marfa stores the choice and the connector follows it, reading `GET /plugins/{name}/connector` on each run. A paused connector's key still writes, so a run under way finishes. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/pause-or-run-a-connector)
- **Added:** An owner can ask a plugin's connector for a preview of how one kind would land under its mapping, or under a draft of it, with `POST /plugins/{name}/connector/previews`. A preview lasts 10 minutes, and a plugin holds at most 20. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/map-a-connector)
- **Added:** The start-only settings `MARFA_CLOUD_URL`, the Marfa Cloud service an instance links to, and `MARFA_CLOUDFLARED`, the path of the tunnel connector when it is not beside the server. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/instance-settings)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa cloud link` prints a code and an approval page and waits until the link is made, `marfa cloud status` reads the link, and `marfa cloud unlink` ends it or cancels one that waits for approval. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/marfa-cloud)
- **Added:** `marfa plugins sign-in` prints the address to open to sign a plugin's connector in to its provider, and with `--wait` waits for that sign-in to end. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/connector-google-access)
- **Added:** `marfa plugins pause`, `resume`, `run` and `status` control a plugin's connector, and `marfa plugins mapping preview` asks it for a preview, with `--wait` to read the answer. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/pause-or-run-a-connector)

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** `@withmarfa/client` types the Marfa Cloud link, connector sign-in, pause, resume, run now and mapping preview operations.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.93...v0.0.94

A plugin's connector can now run on a connector host the owner links once, with its settings, secrets and mapping kept in Marfa, and a synced folder stranded by a restore into a new instance can now be removed without losing track of its edits.

### Server
- **Added:** An owner can make a connector host, one machine that runs connectors, and link it once with a one-time link that expires after 15 minutes. Each plugin's connector is assigned to a host, which mints that connector's own key. Removing a plugin stops its connector and says what went and what stayed. Connectors that register themselves with `POST /connectors` keep working. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/connect-a-service)
- **Added:** A plugin's connector can declare settings, and Marfa keeps their values. The owner reads and sets them with `connectors.manage`, and the connector reads them from its own registration. A secret is sealed on the server and is only ever given back to that connector's own key. An export names each secret without its value, so after a restore onto another machine you set it again.
- **Added:** An owner can set a plugin connector's mapping: for each kind it brings, whether it comes in, the type and tier it lands as, its status words and where each field gets its value. On a type the connector does not own, its key writes and reads only the items under its own source, and its new items land at the mapping's tier, `feed` unless you choose otherwise.
- **Added:** `PUT` and `DELETE /items/{id}/extensions/{namespace}` take an optional `read_revision`, and every extension read returns the namespace's `revision`. When someone else changed the namespace since you read it, the write is refused `409 version_conflict` with the current value, and nothing changes.
- **Fixed:** When every database write fails, such as on a full disk, the attention check still runs, so a webhook listening for `attention.raised` hears about it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa hosts add`, `list`, `get`, `link` and `remove` manage connector hosts, and `marfa plugins assign` gives a plugin's connector to a host. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Added:** `marfa plugins settings` shows and sets a plugin connector's settings, `marfa plugins secret` sets a secret from standard input or a prompt that does not echo, and `marfa plugins mapping show`, `set` and `rewrite` manage its mapping. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Fixed:** After a restore into a new instance at the same address, `marfa folders remove` now takes a folder with unsent edits off the list, keeps its files, and names every file holding a change it could not send, with numbered steps to send those changes to the new instance. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/keep-folder-edits-after-a-restore)

### Core
- **Fixed:** An item recreated after the server was restored from an older backup keeps the source it was made under, instead of moving to the key's own source or being refused.
- **Fixed:** A create resent under another key is read by its ID first, so a lost answer no longer lets the resend overwrite someone else's later edit.
- **Fixed:** An extension write carries the revision you read, so a refused write is held as a conflict with your value kept, and a resend after a lost answer does not block itself.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** `@withmarfa/client` types the connector host, plugin connector settings and mapping operations, and the extension `read_revision` parameter.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.92...v0.0.93

An owner can now install plugins, each app's own `app.<vendor>` data is kept to that app, and `app.*` items are hidden from lists and search as `system.*` items are. This release also carries everything planned for 0.0.91, which was never published.

**Breaking:** The `marfa` command line and the Rust core (the Swift package's working copy) refuse a server older than 0.0.91, so upgrade your server to 0.0.92 with or before them. The listing and search token `include=system` is now `include=hidden`, with no alias. An app's `content` or `*` scope no longer reaches `app.*` data: an app reaches its own vendor without naming it, and another app's only through a grant that names `app.<vendor>.*` or `app.*`. A device now declares only `app.*` types. Type provenance reads `registered` where it read `user`. `POST /types` refuses a new `common.*` type, which arrives only by installing a plugin. Exports are now archive version 2, which earlier releases cannot restore. The upgrade changes how the database is laid out, so it keeps a copy first.

### Server
- **Added:** An owner can install a plugin, a bundle of types, the edge types they use and an optional connector, in one write with `POST /plugins`, and list, read and remove plugins with `GET /plugins`, `GET /plugins/{name}` and `DELETE /plugins/{name}`. A newer version of a plugin may only add to what the installed version published, and removing a plugin keeps its types and items. Each install keeps the SHA-256 of the bundle it received. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Added:** A type's provenance names the plugin and version that installed it, and `common` is reserved for the shared type families that plugins bring. `user.*` holds the owner's own types. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/define-a-type)
- **Added:** An `app.<vendor>` namespace belongs to the app that registered the first type under it. Only the owner moves a vendor to another app, with `PUT /app-vendors/{vendor}`, and `GET /app-vendors` lists who holds each one. On upgrade, a vendor that one app's types alone fill goes to that app, and any other vendor is held for the owner to give. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/access)
- **Changed:** `app.*` items are left out of every list, search, count, view and the overview unless a request asks for `include=hidden` or names the type exactly. A wildcard such as `app.acme.*` opens no hidden type. The bin, exports and backups still carry them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/list-filter-search)
- **Changed:** Only installing a plugin or the owner's own credentials write a type's guidance. An app, or a key an app made, is refused guidance even with `schema.write`.
- **Changed:** Each release archive also carries Cloudflare's tunnel connector, `cloudflared`, pinned and checked by its SHA-256. Nothing runs it in this release.
- **Fixed:** A claim reads an `email` of `null` as no email, and refuses an empty one naming the field, as `PATCH /profile` does.
- **Fixed:** A server whose `MARFA_DATABASE_PATH` is a `file:` URI with `mode=rwc` now starts.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa plugins install` installs a plugin by name from the newest withmarfa/plugins release, or from a bundle file or source folder, and checks the bundle's SHA-256. `list`, `get` and `remove` manage installed plugins, and `check`, `bundle` and `index` work offline. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Added:** `marfa apps vendors list` shows which app holds each `app.<vendor>` namespace, and `marfa apps vendors move` gives one to another app. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Fixed:** A Docker install made under a umask such as `002` keeps its install folder private, so the next install into that folder is admitted.

### Core
- **Changed:** A working copy keeps the `app.*` items it holds, and leaves them out of local lists and search unless the request names their type exactly. Its bin shows them as the server's bin does.
- **Fixed:** A queued write no longer goes out while restored rows are held, or ahead of a kept write.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Added:** `@withmarfa/client` types the plugin and app vendor operations, and its listing options take `include=hidden` in place of `include=system`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.90...v0.0.92

Types can now carry guidance for agents and app builders, `marfa types check` judges a folder of type definitions offline, and an owner can extend any key's life and see every webhook.

**Breaking:** A type registration that names `compatible_with` is now refused `400 invalid_schema`; remove the key, and use `parent` where a type's items should read as another type. A type's `description` over 200 characters, or a field's over 300, is refused, and an edge type property of type `array` with no `items_type`, or of type `enum` with no `enum_values`, is refused. Types and edge types already stored keep reading and restore as they were, but the next replacement of a type must bring its descriptions within the limits.

### Server
- **Added:** A type can carry optional `guidance`, Markdown of up to 1,000 characters that tells an agent or an app builder how to use it. `GET /types/{id}` also returns the guidance of the types above it. Adding, changing or removing guidance needs `schema.write`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/define-a-type)
- **Added:** A status word can carry a description of up to 120 characters, read on every type that inherits it.
- **Added:** An owner can extend a live key's life: a caller with `keys.manage` can send `PATCH /keys/{id}` with a later `expires_at`, or `null`, for any key, including one an app made. The key keeps its secret, and a caller with its own expiry can't extend a key past it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/access)
- **Added:** A credential with both `keys.manage` and `webhooks.manage` can list, read and delete every webhook subscription, whichever app or key made it, including one whose key was revoked or expired. Only a subscription's maker can change it or redeliver. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/receive-webhooks)
- **Changed:** Search ranks an item whose title matches the query above one that only mentions it elsewhere. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/list-filter-search)
- **Changed:** Descriptions have length limits: a type's at most 200 characters, and a field's or an entry member's at most 300.
- **Fixed:** `POST /edge-types` refuses an edge property that a type's field would also be refused for: an `array` with no `items_type`, an `enum` with no `enum_values`, or `enum_values` on a property that is not an enum. Before, these registered, and such an `enum` took any string. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/edges)
- **Removed:** `compatible_with` on types. A type's items are read as another type only through its `parent`.

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa types check FOLDER` judges a folder of `<id>.json` type definitions as a server would at registration, with no server, key or network, and exits non-zero when one is refused. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Added:** `marfa types register`, `replace` and `normalize` with `--file PATH.json` send `PATH.md` beside it as the type's guidance, and `marfa types get` prints a type's guidance and that of the types above it.
- **Added:** `marfa keys update` with `--expires-at`, `--expires-in` or `--no-expiry` extends a key's life with an owner key that holds `keys.manage`.

### Core
- **Changed:** Search on the device ranks a title match above a body match, as the server does.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.89...v0.0.90

A database from 0.0.86 or 0.0.87 now upgrades in place, synced folders keep a note while any file in the folder still carries it, and a folder whose server has been replaced stops and says why instead of asking the server many times a second.

**Breaking:** This release can't open a database that 0.0.88 made, and `marfa server upgrade` refuses it and changes nothing. If you run 0.0.88, export your data with `marfa export` while 0.0.88 runs, make a new install of this release, and restore the archive there with `marfa restore`. From 0.0.86 or 0.0.87, run `marfa server upgrade`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/export-and-restore)

### Server
- **Fixed:** `marfa server upgrade` moves a database from 0.0.86 or 0.0.87 to this release in place, keeping a copy as `marfa.db.before-upgrade` first, with no export and restore. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/upgrade)

### CLI
- **Changed:** `marfa folders watch <DIR>` ends with exit 4 and the code `instance_changed` when the folder's server now answers as another Marfa instance, and `marfa folders status` says why the watch stopped in a new `watch_stopped` field. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-sync-status)

### Core
- **Fixed:** A synced folder no longer moves a note to the bin while a file in the folder still carries it, such as a file held for a name clash or one the folder doesn't send. The scan counts it as `carried`, and a new file at the note's old path waits until the carrying file is renamed or deleted. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** A folder watch whose server has been replaced by another Marfa instance stops that folder, says to add the folder again with a key for the new instance, and keeps the other folders syncing, instead of asking the server hundreds of times a second. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** Folder passes that keep failing, such as against a server that can't be reached, wait from 1 second up to 5 minutes between tries, and a change on disk or the server answering again ends the wait. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/keep-folders-syncing)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.88...v0.0.89

An AI agent at `/mcp/admin` can now do what the API lets the same credential do, from ending a sign-in to updating the server, and synced folders no longer lose what a program writes to an open file or write the same item differently on two computers.

### Server
- **Added:** An agent at `/mcp/admin` can end a browser sign-in or an app, or remove a passkey, with `marfa_end_sign_in`. The first call previews what goes, and a second call with the preview's token does it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Added:** An agent at `/mcp/admin` can remove one store's copy of a file with `marfa_remove_file_copy` and adopt the backup folder with `marfa_adopt_backup_folder`, each after a preview and a confirmation. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Added:** An agent can update the server with `marfa_update_server` and confirm the server's clock with the `confirm_clock` action of `marfa_maintain`, each after a preview and a confirmation. Both appear in the audit log. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** An app whose owner signed in recently can change `allow_private_addresses`, `backup_path` and the object store destination through `marfa_change_settings`, as `PATCH /config` allows. Past the recent sign-in window, the app is asked to have the person sign in again on its next connection. `sign_in_address` stays off MCP and is refused with `not_offered_over_mcp`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** Each MCP endpoint has its own instructions, and every tool carries all four hints. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** The `in-folder` edge has a `form` property, which says how the file writes its frontmatter, with no values. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/catalog/edges/in-folder)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa folders kept <DIR>` lists the files a pull set aside because a program might still have been writing to them. `--discard` deletes the unchanged ones and puts back the changed ones. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Fixed:** `marfa server run` makes every file and folder it creates without a mode of its own private, and folders it creates above the install folder are `0755` rather than `0700`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/install)

### Core
- **Fixed:** A folder pull no longer replaces a file that a program holds open for writing, so nothing the program writes afterward is lost. The pull leaves the file and writes it once the program closes it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** A second directory that follows a folder writes each file the way the first one did, keeping its key order, empty keys, dates and list style, so both computers hold the same bytes. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/work-with-folder-files)
- **Fixed:** A folder narrowed beneath one of its own files holds nothing else from the server while that file waits for its item, even when the key can't change the folder. `marfa folders status` says why the path waits. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/sync-a-folder)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.87...v0.0.88

An install now changes release only through `marfa server upgrade`, which first checks that the new release opens the install's database, in either direction. You can also pause one synced directory, see which part of a directory can't be watched, and open a saved file in the right app because its name now has its type's extension.

**Breaking:** `marfa server install`, `start` and `restart` no longer change an install's release. Given another release's programs, for example after `brew upgrade marfa` or the install script, they change nothing, exit with status 2 and name `marfa server upgrade --dir <dir>`: run that instead. When only a release up to 0.0.85 has served the database, `start` and `restart` can't tell which release the install is on and refuse; run `marfa server upgrade` once to move it. Upgrade the command line and the server together: a server before this release refuses a folder health report that says a directory is paused or partly unwatched.

### Server
- **Added:** A folder's health report can say a directory is `paused` or that part of it is `unwatched`, with the count of directories it can't watch. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Changed:** A server names the release it runs in `marfa.db.release` beside its database once it serves, so the command line knows which release an install is on even while it is stopped. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/upgrade)
- **Fixed:** A restore that refuses an archive with no format or another format, as every release before 0.0.72 wrote, says which build or format it found. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/export-and-restore)

### CLI
- **Added:** `marfa folders pause <DIR>` stops a directory's sync, through a restart or a reboot, until `marfa folders resume <DIR>`, without removing its folder. `folders status` and `folders list` show a paused directory. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/change-or-stop-a-folder)
- **Changed:** `marfa server upgrade` moves an install to a newer or an older release. It first asks that release whether it opens the install's settings and database, and changes nothing when it says no; it then gives the commands that put the earlier release back. With Docker, `--release` may name an earlier image from 0.0.76 on. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/upgrade)
- **Changed:** `marfa server status` shows a `Programs` line when the installed programs belong to a release waiting for `upgrade`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/upgrade#go-back-to-an-earlier-release)

### Core
- **Added:** An app can pause and resume one synced directory through the Swift and Node bindings. A paused directory is refused with `sync_paused` by every command that reads or writes either side, and a watch that is running waits until it is resumed. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/change-or-stop-a-folder)
- **Changed:** A directory that can't watch part of itself no longer says it is in step. It names that part and looks at just those files every 30 seconds instead of walking the whole directory. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** A file item whose title has no extension is written with the extension its type needs, so a PDF titled "Boiler receipt" appears as `Boiler receipt.pdf`. Its title doesn't change, and a file already written keeps its name. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/work-with-folder-files)
- **Fixed:** When a build refuses a working copy or a directory's saved state that another build made, the message names the release that last saved it and, while changes still wait to be sent, how to install that release to send them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.86...v0.0.87

The owner now signs in with a username, telemetry is set from any app with no restart and now includes metrics, an agent at `/mcp/admin` can purge the trash and remove connectors with a confirmation, and a device keeps the work a server restored from a backup lost.

**Breaking:** The owner claims and signs in with a username, not an email: a client that sends `email` to claim or sign in is refused, and the email is now an optional profile field. The server no longer reads the `OTEL_*` variables, `MARFA_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO` or `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`: after you upgrade, set the `otel_` stored settings and `telemetry_enabled` with `marfa config update --file -`. The `error_webhook_url` setting is gone: to hear of faults, follow `attention.raised` with a webhook. A type that sets `enum_values` on a field or column that is not an `enum` is refused with `400 invalid_schema`. The command line no longer reads `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` or `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`.

### Server
- **Added:** An agent connected at `/mcp/admin` can purge chosen items or a page of the trash, delete a connector, clear a connector's state and retire an inbound endpoint. Each act shows a preview first and runs only with a single-use confirmation, and it changes nothing if what it would remove changed in the meantime. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Added:** A new instance can be claimed in the sign-in page that an AI client opens when it connects, and the person then lands on that client's approval page already signed in. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/claude-and-chatgpt)
- **Added:** The server exports request duration and memory use as OpenTelemetry metrics, to `otel_exporter_otlp_metrics_endpoint` or `v1/metrics` under the base endpoint. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Added:** The server lists its own faults in what needs the owner's attention and announces each new one at once as `attention.raised`, even when the database cannot be written. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/receive-webhooks)
- **Added:** A tag replace at `PUT /items/{id}/tags` can name the tags the client read in `read_tags`, and is refused with `409 version_conflict` when another writer changed them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/write-safely)
- **Changed:** The owner signs in with a username, and can change it later at `PATCH /profile` without losing passkeys, sessions, keys or app access. Apps read it through the new `username` profile permission. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/sign-in-as-the-owner)
- **Changed:** The OpenTelemetry settings are stored settings that any app or key with `config.manage` can change, and a change takes effect with no restart. `telemetry_enabled` pauses all telemetry without clearing secrets. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Changed:** A sign-in counts as recent for 15 minutes instead of 5.
- **Changed:** `/mcp/admin` advertises every permission its tools need, so a client approved with full access sees every admin tool. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** An update downloads only from Marfa's release address on GitHub, starts only for a credential that still holds `instance.maintain`, puts the old release back when the new one fails to start, and reports an update that did not finish instead of calling it `succeeded`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/upgrade)
- **Changed:** An app the owner signed in to can widen a key with `keys.mint`, and make a key that outlives the app's own access with `owner_key`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-keys)
- **Fixed:** An object store that `allow_private_addresses` now refuses is reported as unusable in `/health`, `/attention` and `/blobs/stores`, and nothing is purged while it is refused. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Fixed:** When a file's bytes change, what was read from the old bytes (its text, size and length) is cleared so that it is read again.
- **Fixed:** An item's preview and a name taken from its body read as a reader reads the text, without front matter, footnotes, highlight markers or table pipes.
- **Fixed:** A server keeps sole use of its database, blob folder and backup folder even when someone removes its `.server-lock` file, so a second server can no longer start on the same folder.
- **Fixed:** A Linux user install no longer fails to start because the server made its `data` folder writable by other accounts.
- **Removed:** The `error_webhook_url` setting.

### CLI
- **Changed:** `marfa setup claim` takes `--username`, with `--email` optional, and `marfa profile update` takes `--username`, `--email` and `--clear-email`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/cli)
- **Changed:** The `marfa folders` commands say what happened in plain words, `folders add --folder` takes a folder's title as well as its ID, and `folders inventory` shows each folder's title. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/sync-a-folder)
- **Changed:** Messages name apps and actors, give the request ID to quote, print a failed start's log line by line, and say when a store is read only.
- **Removed:** PostHog events from the command line. It still exports OTLP traces through the standard `OTEL_*` variables. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/client-telemetry)

### Core
- **Added:** When a server is restored to an earlier point, a device keeps the items, edges, tags, deletions and table rows the server lost, and queues them back blocked `server_restored` until the person releases or withdraws them. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Added:** A folder can narrow beneath a project that is one of its own files, from the first sync. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/folder-rules)
- **Fixed:** A folder replaces or removes a file only after proving it is the file it read, so a save an editor makes in the meantime is kept, and reported as `kept`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)
- **Fixed:** When two directories on one computer follow the same folder and its query narrows, each keeps its own file of an item the query left out.
- **Fixed:** An edit read from a new item before its create was taken is no longer refused `invalid` once the create is taken. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/write-in-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A tag replace over tags another writer changed is blocked as a conflict, and the copy keeps what the person wrote.

### TypeScript SDK
- **Fixed:** `@withmarfa/client` loads through `require` as well as `import`, so a CommonJS project such as a Raycast extension can use it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/typescript-script)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.84...v0.0.86

The server's PostHog error tracking is now two stored settings you can change from any app with no restart, a device copy renews its sign-in instead of signing a person out when a long read outlasts its token, and queued writes and stores opened by a path are kept safer.

**Breaking:** The server no longer reads `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` or `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`. If you send your server's faults to PostHog, set `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token` together after you upgrade, with `marfa config update --file -`. A self-hosted PostHog must serve the capture v1 endpoint. On a Mac, a working copy opened by a plain path on an NFS, SMB, AFP or WebDAV volume is now refused: keep the store on a local disk.

### Server
- **Added:** The stored settings `posthog_host` and `posthog_project_token` send a report of each server fault to PostHog's error tracking. They are set together, take effect from the next fault, are never shown back, and a host on a private address needs `allow_private_addresses`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/telemetry)
- **Changed:** `error_reporting_enabled` can be on only when `error_webhook_url` or the PostHog pair is set. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/settings)
- **Changed:** Traces, log records and fault reports carry the server's release as `service.version`, and the server no longer calls itself `production` unless `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` says so. A fault report names its trace when traces are exported.
- **Changed:** A health check or a quick read that went well is no longer exported as an OTLP log record. Its line in the request log on standard output stays.
- **Removed:** The `MARFA_POSTHOG_HOST` and `MARFA_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` environment variables, for the server. The command line still reads them.

### Core
- **Fixed:** A catch-up or a hydration whose sign-in token expires while it reads the event stream renews the sign-in and reads on from the last event it took. Before, it ended `stream_incomplete` with `credential_ended`, and a Swift app signed the person out. A copy that holds a key, or a sign-in that has ended, still ends the call. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Fixed:** A queued write is synced to the store's log on every commit, so it survives the app or the system stopping. On a Mac, a sudden power cut can still lose the last writes the drive had not stored, and the store stays whole. Writes and hydration take a little longer. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Fixed:** A store opened through a symbolic link keeps its lock, its file bytes and any set-aside copy beside the file the link leads to, so an upload queued through one name is no longer lost through the other.
- **Changed:** A store opened by a plain path is refused on a file system that does not lock files, or where SQLite cannot use write-ahead mode, instead of risking two writers. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A read that is stopped starts no further request or sign-in renewal.

### Swift SDK
- **Fixed:** A long hydration or catch-up no longer signs a person out when the access token expires mid-read, once the Swift package moves to this release.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.83...v0.0.84

An agent at `/mcp/admin` can now do the owner tasks its permissions open, signing out ends an app's access even after a renewal, and working copies and synced folders keep people's data safer when the server, the credential or the folder changes underneath them.

**Breaking:** With `object_store_path_style` set to `false`, an object store endpoint whose host ends in more than one dot, or has an empty label or a label longer than 63 characters, is now refused with `400` at `/config`, and a stored one attaches no store. Before you upgrade, check `object_store_endpoint` and write the host with at most one dot at its end.

### Server
- **Added:** An agent connected at `/mcp/admin` can read the owner's state and make the owner's guarded changes that its credential's permissions open: settings, the trash, apps, backups, maintenance, connectors, files and sign-ins, with the same rules and refusals as the API. Destructive acts, such as emptying the trash or revoking an app, are not offered. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/marfa-mcp-server)
- **Changed:** A webhook delivery checks that its key still stands after connecting to the receiver and before sending, and sends nothing when it no longer does. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/receive-webhooks)
- **Fixed:** Revoking an app's refresh token at `POST /oauth/revoke` ends the app's grant whenever the token has not ended or expired, even if a later renewal already replaced it. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-apps)
- **Fixed:** `GET /health` reports `blob_storage` as `down` when the blob folder belongs to another store, and a `blob-orphans` run counts a blob as purged once its record is gone.
- **Fixed:** An object store host with several dots at its end is counted at its true length against the 253-character limit.

### CLI
- **Fixed:** `marfa folders confirm` scans the folder again before it lets go of a paused removal. A file that came back under another name keeps its item, and a file it cannot check is reported in `unsure` and never moved to the bin. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/fix-a-folder)

### Core
- **Fixed:** A working copy confirms that the server at its address is still its own instance before it sends item IDs, file hashes or names, and again after a credential renewal. When another instance answers, it sends nothing more and ends `copy_expired` with the reason `instance_changed`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** A write whose answer was lost is read back before it is sent again under a different credential, so an edit is no longer applied twice and a delete that landed is no longer shown as refused. A removal or a create the read cannot settle safely stays queued instead of being sent. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Fixed:** A synced folder's quick check walks the folder where no change event can arrive, such as a directory the system will not watch or a file with another hard link, so those changes are no longer missed until the next full pass.

### Swift SDK
- **Fixed:** A crash inside the core during a call reaches the app as `MarfaError.fault`, instead of an error the app could not match or as `store`, once the Swift package moves to this release. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/reference/swift-sdk/errors-and-testing)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.82...v0.0.83

Object stores addressed by virtual host now work, changing where files and backups go asks for a recent sign-in, and narrowing an app also ends the keys it made that hold more.

**Breaking:** Changing `backup_path` or any `object_store_` setting now needs a sign-in from the last five minutes: an API key is refused with `403 app_sign_in_required`, so use `marfa config set` on the machine where the server runs, or an app after a fresh sign-in. With `object_store_path_style` set to `false`, set `object_store_endpoint` to the store's bare host, without the bucket. An `object_store_region` or `object_store_bucket` that is not a valid name is now refused with `400 validation_error`.

### Server
- **Changed:** Changing `backup_path`, `object_store_bucket`, `object_store_endpoint`, `object_store_region`, `object_store_path_style` or `object_store_prefix` needs a recent sign-in, and changing the bucket or the endpoint removes the stored secret access key unless the same change sets one. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Changed:** Narrowing an app's access also revokes every key the app made that reaches beyond the new access, and the answer to `PATCH /grants/{id}` says how many in `revoked_keys`. Keys within the new access keep working. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-apps)
- **Changed:** A restore that would add a setting the instance does not have yet also needs `config.manage`. Without it, the restore is refused with `403` before anything is written, naming the permission and the settings. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Changed:** `object_store_region` and `object_store_bucket` must be valid names, and a write outside the rule is refused with `400 validation_error` naming the setting.
- **Fixed:** An object store with `object_store_path_style` set to `false` is reached at the bucket's own host, `<bucket>.<endpoint host>`, for every request and signed link. Before, the bucket was left out of the address and such a store never worked. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)
- **Fixed:** A stored object store setting that cannot be used no longer stops the server from starting. The server attaches no store, serves files from its disk and names the setting on the attention list until you correct it, with no restart.

### CLI
- **Changed:** `marfa apps narrow` says how many keys it revoked that the app made. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/manage-apps)

### Core
- **Added:** A renewal that an app's credential renewer fails ends with its own error, `renewal_refused`, with a reason an app can word, instead of `invalid`. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/devices)
- **Changed:** Pushing a folder, and the quick check after you edit a file in a large synced folder, do much less work, so changes reach the server sooner.
- **Fixed:** Opening a working copy on a full disk answers `storage_full` instead of `store`, and a store that a newer build made is refused with `wrong_schema` and left exactly as it was. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/build/fix-a-working-copy)
- **Fixed:** On a volume that keeps names apart by case, such as most Linux file systems, a file held beside a note in another case (`Q.md` beside `q.md`) no longer replaces the note's file after the note is moved or retitled. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/use/work-with-folder-files)
- **Fixed:** Stopping a sync ends it at once, instead of waiting up to 30 seconds for a request the sync had already started.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.81...v0.0.82

Backups work as soon as you set where they go, and the docs at docs.marfa.so now describe this release.

### Server
- **Fixed:** Listing, taking or restoring a backup works straight after you set the backup folder or object store, instead of answering that no backup destination is set. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/run/back-up-and-restore)

### CLI
- **Changed:** After `marfa server install`, the hint for connecting an agent points to `marfa docs connect-your-agent`, and the `marfa docs` help names pages that exist. [Docs](https://docs.marfa.so/connect-your-agent)

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/compare/v0.0.80...v0.0.81
